title: American Railways
intro: A hidden study page for the six Amtrak routes shown on a western long-distance route map: the Empire Builder, Coast Starlight, California Zephyr, Southwest Chief, Heartland Flyer and Sunset Limited. Facts below are checked against official Amtrak route pages, the Amtrak timetable PDFs current on 24 Nov 2026, and the official Amtrak Mileage Record dated 17 Jun 2025. Anything not taken from a cited source is marked not collected.

routes.name: Empire Builder
routes.endpoints: Chicago, IL – St. Paul/Minneapolis, MN – Spokane, WA – Portland, OR / Seattle, WA
routes.frequency: Daily, in both directions. The train splits and joins at Spokane: 7/8 continue to and from Seattle; 27/28 continue to and from Portland.
routes.duration: About 46 hours on the official route page. The Amtrak timetable dated 24 Nov 2026 prints 45h 50m (train 8), 46h 0m (train 28), 46h 24m (train 7) and 46h 12m (train 27).
routes.highlights: Glacier National Park, Gassman Coulee Trestle, Columbia River Gorge, Mississippi River views
overview: The Empire Builder is Amtrak’s daily long-distance train between Chicago and the Pacific Northwest. The official route page describes the journey as Chicago – St. Paul/Minneapolis – Spokane – Portland/Seattle, with a published journey time of 46 hours and daily departures.

West of Spokane the train divides. Trains 7 (west) and 8 (east) run Chicago–Seattle; trains 27 (west) and 28 (east) run Chicago–Portland. The 24 Nov 2026 timetable lists all four numbers. Trainside checked bicycles are available on trains 7 and 8 only, not 27 and 28, according to the official route page.

Official scenery notes include views of the Mississippi, the Minneapolis–St. Paul skyline, the North Dakota plains and the Gassman Coulee Trestle, Glacier National Park in Montana, and, on the Portland section, the Columbia River Gorge with views of Mt. Hood and Beacon Rock.

stations.name: East Glacier Park
stations.note: Listed on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable with no times printed. Whether service is seasonal on this date is not collected from a printed footnote.

stations.name: Spokane
stations.note: The Seattle and Portland sections split and join here.

parks_sourced.name: Glacier National Park
parks_sourced.note: Named on the official Empire Builder page as a travelers’ favorite that the train passes in Montana. West Glacier and (when served) East Glacier Park are the nearby rail stations.

not_collected: Times for East Glacier Park (GPK) on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable extract (the station is listed, but no times are printed; a seasonal footnote was not collected from that extract).
Driving distances from stations to the national parks that appear only on the submitted map.
Whether Yellowstone, Grand Teton, Theodore Roosevelt, Badlands or Wind Cave are presented as official Amtrak connections for this train.

routes.name: Coast Starlight
routes.endpoints: Seattle, WA – Portland, OR – Sacramento, CA – Los Angeles, CA
routes.distance: 1,337 miles Los Angeles–Seattle (trains 11/14) in the official Amtrak Mileage Record dated 17 Jun 2025. The same table also lists a second Los Angeles–Seattle figure of 1,372 miles on train 14; which figure Amtrak prints on the consumer route page is not collected.
routes.frequency: Daily, in both directions (timetable dated 24 Nov 2026: train 11 and train 14 both Daily).
routes.duration: About 35 hours on the official route page. The 24 Nov 2026 timetable prints 34h 0m for train 14 and 35h 16m for train 11.
routes.highlights: Cascade Range and Mount Shasta, Pacific shoreline, San Francisco Bay Area, Santa Barbara
overview: The Coast Starlight is Amtrak’s daily train between Seattle and Los Angeles, via Portland, Sacramento and the San Francisco Bay Area. The official route page calls the scenery unsurpassed: snow-covered Cascade peaks and Mount Shasta, forests, valleys and long stretches of Pacific shoreline.

Train 11 runs Seattle–Los Angeles; train 14 runs Los Angeles–Seattle. Both are marked Daily on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable. The official page also highlights the Klamath Falls–Dunsmuir corridor and travel through the Cascades at 5,000 feet, and destination notes for San Luis Obispo.

stations.name: Burbank
stations.note: Train 14 is printed with no scheduled stop at Burbank on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable; train 11 is timed.

not_collected: Which of the two Los Angeles–Seattle mileages in the 17 Jun 2025 Mileage Record (1,337 and 1,372) is the consumer-page figure.
Driving distances from stations to parks labeled only on the submitted map.
Whether Joshua Tree is an official Amtrak-listed highlight of this route (the official Coast Starlight page text retrieved for this build does not name it).

routes.name: California Zephyr
routes.endpoints: Chicago, IL – Omaha, NE – Denver, CO – Salt Lake City, UT – Emeryville, CA (San Francisco)
routes.distance: 2,438 miles Chicago–Emeryville (trains 5/6), official Amtrak Mileage Record dated 17 Jun 2025
routes.frequency: Daily, in both directions (timetable dated 24 Nov 2026).
routes.duration: 51 hours 20 minutes on the official route page. The 24 Nov 2026 timetable prints 52h 14m for train 6 and 52h 57m for train 5.
routes.highlights: Colorado Rockies, Sierra Nevada, Denver, Salt Lake City, connections to San Francisco from Emeryville
overview: The California Zephyr is Amtrak’s daily long-distance train between Chicago and Emeryville (for San Francisco), via Omaha, Denver and Salt Lake City. The official route page describes the climb through the Rockies and the Sierra Nevada and notes connecting bus service from Emeryville into San Francisco and Oakland.

Train 5 runs west toward Emeryville; train 6 runs east toward Chicago. Both are Daily on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable. The same timetable lists the intermediate rail stations used in the table below, including Grand Junction, Glenwood Springs, Denver, Omaha and Lincoln — stations also labeled on the submitted western-route map.
not_collected: Official Amtrak text linking this train to each park labeled on the submitted map (the official page describes the Rockies and the Sierra Nevada in general terms).
Driving distances from stations such as Granby, Glenwood Springs, Grand Junction or Green River to nearby parks.

routes.name: Southwest Chief
routes.endpoints: Chicago, IL – Kansas City, MO – Albuquerque, NM – Flagstaff, AZ – Los Angeles, CA
routes.distance: 2,264 miles Chicago–Los Angeles (trains 3/4), official Amtrak Mileage Record dated 17 Jun 2025
routes.frequency: Daily, in both directions (timetable dated 24 Nov 2026).
routes.duration: “40+ hours” on the official route page. The 24 Nov 2026 timetable prints 43h 49m for train 4 and 43h 57m for train 3.
routes.highlights: Raton Pass, New Mexico pueblos and high desert, Flagstaff / Grand Canyon Thruway, Kansas City

osm_relations.label: Chicago → Los Angeles (simplified geometry already used on the existing Southwest Chief page)

overview: The Southwest Chief is Amtrak’s daily long-distance train between Chicago and Los Angeles, via Kansas City, Albuquerque and Flagstaff. The official route page describes travel across eight states, through canyon passages, wheat fields, ranches, missions, pueblos, mountains and deserts.

This hidden American Railways subpage is a concise entry for the route. A fuller, already published set of notes, station pages and a live tracker is at the existing Southwest Chief section of this site. Use those pages for station-level times, the Lamy timetable discussion, and the working Amtraker tracker.

The submitted western-route map labeled Flagstaff, Williams, Albuquerque, Lamy and Kansas City, with trains 3 and 4. Williams Junction (WMJ) appears on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable with no scheduled stop. Do not treat Williams as a current rail stop unless Amtrak publishes times for it.

parks_sourced.name: Grand Canyon National Park
parks_sourced.note: The existing Southwest Chief page on this site records Flagstaff Thruway connections toward the Grand Canyon. Use that page rather than inventing a new transfer description here.

not_collected: A current scheduled stop at Williams / Williams Junction (WMJ is printed on the 24 Nov 2026 timetable with no times).
Driving distances from Winslow, Gallup or other stations to Petrified Forest or Mesa Verde.
Anything already marked not collected on the existing Southwest Chief station pages, including the Lamy 12:49 PM vs official 12:53 PM question, which is not re-decided here.

routes.name: Heartland Flyer
routes.endpoints: Oklahoma City, OK – Fort Worth, TX
routes.distance: Official mileage is not collected: the Heartland Flyer is not listed in the 17 Jun 2025 Amtrak Mileage Record retrieved for this build. Wikipedia’s List of Amtrak routes and the OpenStreetMap Texas/Railroads wiki both publish 206 miles; treat that figure as secondary until an official Amtrak mileage line is collected.
routes.frequency: Daily, in both directions (official route page and the 24 Nov 2026 timetable).
routes.duration: 4 hours 14 minutes on the official route page. The 24 Nov 2026 timetable prints 4h 2m for both train 821 and train 822.
routes.highlights: A daily Oklahoma–Texas link, with Texas Eagle connections at Fort Worth

osm_relations.label: Oklahoma City → Fort Worth (directional relation used for geometry)

overview: The Heartland Flyer is Amtrak’s daily state-supported train between Oklahoma City and Fort Worth. The official route page says the service connects Oklahoma City to Fort Worth daily and that, at Fort Worth, connections are available to Dallas, Chicago and San Antonio via the Texas Eagle. The page also states that the service is financed primarily through funds made available by the Oklahoma and Texas Departments of Transportation.

The submitted map labeled the route Oklahoma City to Fort Worth and showed train 821. Official numbers are 821 and 822. On the 24 Nov 2026 timetable, train 821 is timed from Oklahoma City (8:25a) to Fort Worth (12:27p) and train 822 from Fort Worth (5:25p) to Oklahoma City (9:27p).
not_collected: An official Amtrak mileage for Oklahoma City–Fort Worth (not present in the 17 Jun 2025 Mileage Record used here).

National-park associations for this short corridor (none were named on the official route page text retrieved for this build, and none were required from the submitted map’s park list as a station-to-park fact).

routes.name: Sunset Limited
routes.endpoints: New Orleans, LA – San Antonio, TX – Tucson, AZ – Maricopa, AZ (for Phoenix) – Los Angeles, CA
routes.distance: 1,994 miles New Orleans–Los Angeles (trains 1/2), official Amtrak Mileage Record dated 17 Jun 2025
routes.frequency: Three departures a week in each direction. The official route page says “Departures Three Days a Week.” The 24 Nov 2026 timetable prints train 1 as MoWeSa (westbound, New Orleans–Los Angeles) and train 2 as SuWeFr (eastbound, Los Angeles–New Orleans).
routes.duration: About 48 hours on the official route page. The 24 Nov 2026 timetable prints 46h 35m for train 1 and 45h 40m for train 2.
routes.highlights: Bayou country, southwestern deserts, Mexican border, California mountains; Phoenix connection from Maricopa
overview: The Sunset Limited is Amtrak’s southernmost long-distance train, between New Orleans and Los Angeles via San Antonio, El Paso, Tucson and Maricopa (for Phoenix). The official route page describes Bayou Country, the Mexican border, southwestern deserts and California mountains, and states that three trains depart weekly in each direction.

Train 1 runs west; train 2 runs east. The official page also notes Amtrak Connection service between the Maricopa, AZ station and Phoenix Metro Center, Phoenix Airport and Tempe. The submitted map labeled Maricopa, Tucson, El Paso and San Antonio, with trains 1 and 2.

stations.name: Maricopa
stations.note: Amtrak Connection service to the Phoenix area is described on the official Sunset Limited page.

parks_sourced.name: Joshua Tree National Park
parks_sourced.note: The official Sunset Limited page’s Palm Springs destination text says you can take a drive to Joshua Tree National Park.

not_collected: Driving distances from Tucson to Saguaro, from Alpine or El Paso to Big Bend or Guadalupe Mountains, or from other stations to Carlsbad Caverns.

Whether Saguaro, Carlsbad Caverns, Guadalupe Mountains or Big Bend are named on the official Sunset Limited page (the retrieved page text names Joshua Tree from Palm Springs; the others were labeled on the submitted map only).
